title: Link-writable source and audit evidence
evidence: COOL and the inspected review environment file both return anyone/writer permissions. Link discovery is disabled, not link access.
impact: Anyone obtaining the link can affect source integrity; evidence files and hashes in the same editable boundary do not independently establish authenticity.
recommendation: Restrict access to named accounts, preserve a trusted snapshot, review change/access evidence, and segregate sensitive source and immutable release evidence. No permissions were changed during this audit.

title: Review credentials in the shared workspace
evidence: The review environment file contains a nonempty review identity and OTP, signing account identifiers and a local key-file path. No secret values are reproduced.
impact: An active review credential could expose the review account; identifiers and a path are not proof that private signing key bytes leaked.
recommendation: Test validity through the authorized account owner, revoke active review access, inspect related sessions and distribution, remove sensitive material from shared delivery copies, and inventory ignored files and archives as well as Git.

title: Two conflicting Increment 11 candidates, no canonical integrated release
evidence: Both branches have 112 source paths; 108 overlap, 104 match, four shared paths differ and each branch has four exclusive paths. Original AGENTS remains unrevised.
impact: Applying packages by date or folder name can lose fixes; a checksum proves transport integrity, not correctness or integration.
recommendation: Choose a protected canonical checkout, review the four shared conflicts and eight exclusive files, retain both useful test sets, create one reviewed commit and rebuild every target from it.

title: Latest Dart changes are not application-validated
evidence: Increment receipts explicitly distinguish authored Dart tests from executed tooling tests. SDK-equipped integrated execution for the latest merged candidate was not available.
impact: Compilation errors, API mismatches and runtime regressions can survive string checks and fixture installers.
recommendation: Run pinned formatting, full analysis and all unit/widget tests; build signed production Android, iOS and both web surfaces; preserve command outputs, commit and artifact identity.

title: Git snapshot does not establish a reproducible working checkout
evidence_state: Confirmed index comparison; object completeness unknown
evidence: The Git index contains 1,569 entries. Six of seven compared original files match indexed blobs; the Rwanda-only migration is not present in the index. The inspected pack folder did not expose a matching .pack file.
impact: The Drive snapshot may contain uncommitted work or incomplete object transport. Neither possibility is a proven malicious change.
recommendation: Reconstruct from the authorized source remote, run status/fsck, compare worktree and migration hashes, identify intended changes, and capture exact commit plus reproducible build inputs.

title: Retired design rule remains an active instruction
evidence: Original AGENTS and CI still refer to the retired rule, despite owner instructions and revised candidate policy.
impact: Conflicting instructions can regenerate prohibited checks and block otherwise valid work.
recommendation: Remove active references from the integrated source, scripts and CI; keep historical archives clearly non-authoritative. The revolut-design skill is the sole design authority.

title: Rwanda-only runtime conflicts with dual-rail and AI-only documentation
evidence: README and the 25 September migration are Rwanda-only; architecture, operations and parser documents still mandate bank/diaspora behavior or OpenAI-only SMS parsing.
impact: Operators can deploy retired functions, users can receive inaccurate disclosures, and tests may assert the wrong product contract.
recommendation: Approve one current product matrix and regenerate architecture, public copy, privacy notices, deployment allowlists, operations and test expectations from that agreed scope.

title: Attestation contract downgrade is accepted by Edge code
evidence: Missing contract RPC or a value other than one selects legacy SMS ingestion; finalization also returns legacy_contract when the expected version is absent.
impact: A partially deployed or drifted environment can silently weaken the required receipt-security boundary.
recommendation: Require a supported contract version in production; return unavailable on unknown/missing versions and prove by integration tests that legacy paths cannot post without required authorization and evidence.

title: Auth hook has an alternate static-secret authorization path
evidence: The handler supports both signed-hook verification and an alternate shared-secret path. A production dry-run option can acknowledge without delivery.
impact: A leaked alternate secret or accidental dry-run setting can invalidate assumptions about replay resistance and successful OTP delivery.
recommendation: Use the intended signed webhook route in production; reject stale/replayed/mutated requests, disable dry-run in release configuration and contract-test successful versus failed delivery acknowledgements.

title: OTP abuse and provider failure controls need completion
evidence: The database serializes five requests per phone per ten minutes. It stores IP hashes but this function does not impose an IP/global budget. Provider calls have no explicit timeout in the inspected handler, and error-body logging is bounded but not field-allowlisted.
impact: Distributed phone rotation, provider latency and diagnostic payloads can increase cost, latency or sensitive-data exposure.
recommendation: Add trusted-edge IP/account/global budgets, delivery timeouts and safe structured logging; validate CAPTCHA where appropriate in the custom flow, not merely as a dashboard toggle.

title: Device integrity and parser completeness are not settlement proof
evidence_state: Confirmed parser behavior; financial boundary verification required
evidence: A synthetic arbitrary-sender message with an MTN body hint and a masked payer receives network=mtn_momo and confidence=0.96 without a transaction ID. This does not demonstrate a database posting bypass.
impact: Treating a heuristic parser score or recognized device as verified funds risks false ledger confirmation.
recommendation: Document independent evidence requirements, retain deterministic extraction, enforce unique receiver/payer/amount/time/intent matching, quarantine ambiguity and prove no unauthorized or duplicate posting through transactional tests.

title: Exactly-once financial outcomes lack current end-to-end proof
evidence_state: Current validation gap; positive source controls exist
evidence: Parsing has lease and replay handling, while the architecture assigns allocation and ledger posting to database functions. This audit did not execute the full allocator, reversal or current permission matrix.
impact: Retries, crash windows, collisions and partial deployment may leave duplicate credits, stuck evidence or misleading balances if the complete transaction contract is not proven.
recommendation: Exercise crashes before/after durable ingest, parser insert, allocation, finality and notification; reconcile group/member balances to immutable postings and distinguish receipts, allocated events and confirmed records.

title: Queue capacity and corruption can lose unprocessed receipt evidence
evidence: The native queue is capped at 100. A decryption/read exception deletes encrypted and legacy queues and returns an empty array; failed writes and full queues are logged.
impact: A genuine receipt may never reach the server and may be unrecoverable because inbox backfill is deliberately absent.
recommendation: Persist a non-sensitive loss/corruption indicator; design controlled recovery and capacity management, measure overflow on realistic bursts and never convert evidence loss into payment success. Preserve explicit consent-revocation deletion.

title: Process-local worker is not durable background delivery
evidence_state: Confirmed source; observed device behavior untested
evidence: SmsQueueWorker is a single daemon executor. The receiver raises a queue event; this alone is not a persistent OS upload job.
impact: App termination, reboot, Doze and vendor restrictions can delay or strand receipt ingestion.
recommendation: Define foreground and background guarantees; use a suitable persistent scheduler where supported, constrain it by current owner/consent, and test lifecycle recovery on real MTN/Airtel devices.

title: Native and server capture limits and filters differ
evidence: Native capture uses 2,000 characters and a sender/body-hint filter; server ingestion bounds raw text by bytes, with a 4,096-byte body limit.
impact: Unicode, multipart and altered provider templates can be rejected at different layers; broad body hints are classification, not source authentication.
recommendation: Publish one versioned capture contract and bilingual provider corpus; test UTF-8 limits, mixed multipart senders, duplicate broadcasts, delayed messages and provider-template changes.

title: Response pagination still performs whole-history work
evidence: history_page materializes payment_history JSON, ranks and hashes the matching dataset, and computes aggregates before limiting rows. Recent-intents selection first creates the full intent list.
impact: Per-page database work can grow with total history and may cause repeated refreshes as revisions change during active use.
recommendation: Benchmark query plans on representative isolated datasets; move to indexed relational keyset retrieval and versioned aggregate snapshots where justified, preserving authorization and correctness.

title: Other collection and notification reads need bounded contracts
evidence: The current collection RPC aggregates all visible collections; not every remaining list or notification query was traced to a bounded server contract.
impact: Client-only pagination or hidden caps can truncate lists and produce misleading totals.
recommendation: Inventory each list RPC/query and require stable ordering, filters, explicit total/continuation semantics and scale tests; treat absent aggregates as unavailable rather than fabricated zero.

title: Current hosted schema, grants and function versions are unverified
evidence: The connected Supabase discovery returned no accessible projects. No hosted migration inventory, advisors, policy definitions or function deployment versions could be read.
impact: Source hardening is not proof the deployed backend enforces it; historical readbacks predate later migrations.
recommendation: Obtain read-only access to the exact linked project, compare migrations and function hashes, run catalog-based privilege checks and isolated actor tests before authorizing any release.

title: No-staging guidance and disabled local services leave integration gaps
evidence_state: Confirmed documentation/local configuration; hosted topology unknown
evidence: Readiness guidance says deploy directly to production. Local config disables Realtime and Storage although product flows reference them.
impact: A local pass can omit critical platform dependencies; production becomes the first place to find integration failures.
recommendation: Establish an isolated production-like environment with synthetic accounts and provider sandbox controls; test Realtime, Storage, queues, auth and migrations without real financial side effects.

title: Production-readiness workflow needs a strict trust boundary
evidence: The workflow triggers on pull requests and can expose production credentials when a repository variable enables the linked job. The job has no explicit protected-environment approval or trusted-ref condition in this file.
impact: Same-repository untrusted changes could reach credential-bearing commands if configuration enables that path. Fork secret defaults do not cover all cases.
recommendation: Separate untrusted tests from approved read-only production verification; require protected environment and trusted ref, minimize credentials and prove no PR-controlled code sees production secrets.

title: A green optional-readiness workflow can mean skipped checks
evidence: Both disabled readiness and missing secrets produce successful echo/skip stages. General CI uses a 40% coverage floor, fixture journey smoke and a dev APK size proxy.
impact: A green badge can be mistaken for a tested production backend, signed app or complete financial coverage.
recommendation: Represent required checks as blocked when prerequisites are missing, require production-flavor artifacts, and track high-risk behavioral coverage rather than an overall line percentage alone.

title: Historical CI and screenshot reports contradict the current source
evidence: The September 10 repair report says an evidence-consistency target was removed, but the retrieved original CI still calls it. The same report describes old billing and screenshot-fingerprint blockers.
impact: Teams may rely on fixes from another checkout or stale release evidence. Current billing and hosted run status were not independently verified.
recommendation: Read the canonical remote commit and current workflow runs, resolve the discrepancy, restore healthy hosted CI and recapture screenshots from the same signed candidate being released.

title: Stable JavaScript path has immutable one-year cache policy
evidence: web/_headers marks /main.dart.js immutable for a year. A versioned service-worker registration is present, but final emitted URLs, cache fetch behavior and live headers were not tested.
impact: Users may retain old client code against a newer backend if stable URLs do not change and the HTTP cache bypass is insufficient.
recommendation: Version/hash entrypoint URLs or use revalidation for stable paths, verify service-worker migration/logout cleanup and test an actual vN-to-vN+1 deployment with a warm browser cache.

title: Current recovery acceptance is incomplete
evidence_state: Historical evidence plus current verification gap
evidence: Runbooks report past database restore and upgrade exercises but leave object-byte recovery, independent targets, RPO/RTO and full platform recovery open. Later migrations require new rehearsal.
impact: A recoverable database alone does not restore object evidence, auth authority, provider configuration or safe outbound queues.
recommendation: Set business RPO/RTO; verify current backups/PITR, Storage object backups and off-site copies; rehearse isolated restoration, revoked-session handling and controlled queue reactivation.

title: Financial observability and exception handling need operating evidence
evidence: No current service dashboard, alert-delivery proof, queue age distribution, provider SLA or staffed exception rota was available in the inspected material.
impact: A technically correct but unmonitored queue can leave members waiting and operators unable to explain missing confirmations.
recommendation: Instrument sanitized state-transition metrics, age/dead-letter alerts, reconciliation variances and provider costs; assign an incident commander, operator coverage and escalation rules.

title: Candidate UI improvements are not visual or device acceptance
evidence: Packages contain compact form, lazy-list, recovery and truthful-summary changes. The actual screens were not run under the pinned SDK or reviewed against the installed revolut-design skill.
impact: Keyboard, large text, focus, semantics and error recovery can still fail even when source checks pass.
recommendation: Run all critical journeys on compact/large text screens, real keyboards and assistive technology; verify visible and spoken distinction between prepared, pending, received and confirmed states.

title: Restricted-SMS and release-device approvals are unverified
evidence: The Android workflow depends on restricted receipt permissions and a Play-recognized app/device. The repository itself treats Play approval and physical operator UAT as external gates.
impact: A build can compile but be undistributable or unable to create groups/capture receipts on the intended devices.
recommendation: Verify the actual permission declaration, release signing/package/certificates, Integrity configuration and real SIM behavior; do not assume sideloading or a PWA preserves these capabilities.

title: Operational legal position and data-transfer evidence require confirmation
evidence_state: Evidence gap; no finding of legal violation
evidence: The supplied files do not establish current registration/authorization, processor agreements, retention implementation or a current regulatory perimeter opinion for the deployed Rwanda-only flow.
impact: Non-custodial labeling alone does not resolve data-protection or payment-services obligations. Receipt names, numbers and group affiliation remain sensitive operational data.
recommendation: Commission current Rwanda counsel review of actual control of funds and payment initiation; verify DPO registration/transfer-storage permissions, DPIA, data inventory, rights procedures and accurate notices.

title: Blind deletion of fonts, icons, assets and migrations would be unsafe
evidence_state: Confirmed dependency declarations; full reference coverage incomplete
evidence: The manifest declares Inter/Aeonik and Cupertino icons for reachable platform controls; historical financial migrations retain audit data. The asset manifest and old reports have differing historical counts.
impact: Deleting by extension or age can break native controls, legal font attribution, restore replay or retained financial evidence.
recommendation: Use full import/runtime/bundle reference coverage, document licenses and retained history, remove only proven dead runtime paths, and rebuild before accepting savings claims.

title: Dynamic content exists but needs a governed contract
evidence: Public runtime configuration and settings/flags are present in the workstream. Historical fallback language can still conflict with runtime capability.
impact: Moving every label into a database creates avoidable dependency; silently defaulting financial policy can be unsafe.
recommendation: Keep stable UI labels local; govern capability flags, policy versions and product limits with schemas, safe defaults, authorization, audit trails and rollback. Require real active policy before customer acceptance.

title: Evidence authenticity and release approvals need separation
evidence_state: Confirmed sharing risk plus process gap
evidence: Packages have strong transport hashes and detailed receipts, but live signatures, protected CI outputs and current accountable approval were not validated.
impact: Mutually editable source and evidence can agree while both are wrong; many incremental receipts can obscure unresolved acceptance gates.
recommendation: Create one release manifest linking commit, migrations, functions, tests, screenshots, store artifacts and signoffs; store it under restricted, versioned or immutable control.

title: Do not rewrite Flutter before measuring a platform-specific blocker
evidence: The architecture already uses a native Android receipt/security boundary with shared Flutter member and admin surfaces. No comparative device measurements justify a platform rewrite.
impact: A rewrite would expand scope and reintroduce financial, privacy and navigation regressions before existing work is integrated.
recommendation: Retain Flutter/Supabase for the initial release; optimize measured hot paths and native boundaries. Reconsider a specific surface only with repeatable bottleneck evidence and migration economics.
